## SECTION I

## 1.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 1.1] This Section of this Practice Direction applies to arbitration claims to which Section I of Part 62 applies.

## 1.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 1.2] In this Section ‘the 1996 Act’ means the Arbitration Act 1996.

## 1.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 1.3] Where a rule provides for a document to be sent, it may be sent –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 1.3] (1) by first class post;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 1.3] (2) through a document exchange; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 1.3] (3) by fax, electronic mail or other means of electronic communication.

## 62.3 – Starting the claim

## 2.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.1] An arbitration claim under the 1996 Act (other than under section 9) must be started in accordance with the High Court and County Courts (Allocation of Arbitration Proceedings) Order 1996 by the issue of an arbitration claim form.

## 2.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.2] An arbitration claim form must be substantially in the form set out in Appendix A to this practice direction.

## 2.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.3] Subject to paragraph 2.1, an arbitration claim form –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.3] (1) may be issued at the courts set out in column 1 of the table below and will be entered in the list set out against that court in column 2;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.3] (2) relating to a landlord and tenant or partnership dispute must be issued in the Chancery Division of the High Court.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.3] Court | List

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.3] Admiralty and Commercial Registry at the Royal Courts of Justice, London | Commercial list

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.3] Technology and Construction Court Registry, St. Dunstan’s House, London | TCC list

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.3] District Registry of the High Court (where Circuit Commercial Court established) | Circuit Commercial list

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.3] District Registry of the High Court (where arbitration claim form marked ‘Technology and Construction Court’ in top right hand corner) | TCC list

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.3]  | 

## 2.3A

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 2.3A] An arbitration claim form must, in the case of an appeal, or application for permission to appeal, from a judge-arbitrator, be issued in the Civil Division of the Court of Appeal. The judge hearing the application may adjourn the matter for oral argument before two judges of that court.

## 62.4 – Arbitration claim form

## Service

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > Service] The court may exercise its powers under rule 6.15 to permit service of an arbitration claim form at the address of a party’s solicitor or representative acting for that party in the arbitration.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > Service] Where the arbitration claim form is served by the claimant he must file a certificate of service within 7 days of service of the arbitration claim form.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > Service] (Rule 6.17 specifies what a certificate of service must show).

## Acknowledgment of service or making representations by arbitrator or ACAS

## 4.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.1] Where –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.1] (1) an arbitrator; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.1] (2) ACAS (in a claim under the 1996 Act as applied with modifications by the ACAS Arbitration Scheme (England and Wales) Order 2001)

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.1] is sent a copy of an arbitration claim form (including an arbitration claim form sent under rule 62.6(2)), that arbitrator or ACAS (as the case may be) may –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.1] (a) apply to be made a defendant; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.1] (b) make representations to the court under paragraph 4.3.

## 4.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.2] An application under paragraph 4.1(2)(a) to be made a defendant –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.2] (1) must be served on the claimant; but

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.2] (2) need not be served on any other party.

## 4.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 4.3] An arbitrator or ACAS may make representations by filing written evidence or in writing to the court.

## Supply of documents from court records

## 5.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 5.1] An arbitration claim form may only be inspected with the permission of the court.

## 62.7 – Case management

## 6.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.1] The following directions apply unless the court orders otherwise.

## 6.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.2] A defendant who wishes to rely on evidence before the court must file and serve his written evidence –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.2] (1) within 21 days after the date by which he was required to acknowledge service; or,

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.2] (2) where a defendant is not required to file an acknowledgement of service, within 21 days after service of the arbitration claim form.

## 6.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.3] A claimant who wishes to rely on evidence in reply to written evidence filed under paragraph 6.2 must file and serve his written evidence within 7 days after service of the defendant’s evidence.

## 6.4

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.4] Agreed indexed and paginated bundles of all the evidence and other documents to be used at the hearing must be prepared by the claimant.

## 6.5

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.5] Not later than 5 days before the hearing date estimates for the length of the hearing must be filed together with a complete set of the documents to be used.

## 6.6

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] Not later than 2 days before the hearing date the claimant must file and serve –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] (1) a chronology of the relevant events cross-referenced to the bundle of documents;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] (2) (where necessary) a list of the persons involved; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] (3) a skeleton argument which lists succinctly –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] (a) the issues which arise for decision;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] (b) the grounds of relief (or opposing relief) to be relied upon;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] (c) the submissions of fact to be made with the references to the evidence; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.6] (d) the submissions of law with references to the relevant authorities.

## 6.7

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.7] Not later than the day before the hearing date the defendant must file and serve a skeleton argument which lists succinctly –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.7] (1) the issues which arise for decision;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.7] (2) the grounds of relief (or opposing relief) to be relied upon;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.7] (3) the submissions of fact to be made with the references to the evidence; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 6.7] (4) the submissions of law with references to the relevant authorities.

## Securing the attendance of witnesses

## 7.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 7.1] A party to arbitral proceedings being conducted in England or Wales who wishes to rely on section 43 of the 1996 Act to secure the attendance of a witness must apply for a witness summons in accordance with Part 34.

## 7.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 7.2] If the attendance of the witness is required within the district of a district registry, the application may be made at that registry.

## 7.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 7.3] A witness summons will not be issued until the applicant files written evidence showing that the application is made with –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 7.3] (1) the permission of the tribunal; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 7.3] (2) the agreement of the other parties.

## Interim remedies

## 8.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 8.1] An application for an interim remedy under section 44 of the 1996 Act must be made in an arbitration claim form.

## 9.1 Omitted

## Decisions without a hearing

## 10.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 10.1] Having regard to the overriding objective the court may decide particular issues without a hearing.

## 10.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 10.2] The court will generally decide whether to extend the time limit under section 70(3) of the 1996 Act without a hearing. Where the court makes an order extending the time limit, the defendant must file his written evidence within 21 days from service of the order.

## 62.9 – Variation of time

## 11.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 11.1] An application for an order under rule 62.9(1) –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 11.1] (1) before the period of 28 days has expired, must be made in a Part 23 application notice; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 11.1] (2) after the period of 28 days has expired, must be set out in a separately identified part in the arbitration claim form.

## Applications for permission to appeal

## 12.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.1] Where a party seeks permission to appeal to the court on a question of law arising out of an arbitration award, the arbitration claim form must, in addition to complying with rule 62.4(1) –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.1] (1) identify the question of law;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.1] (2) state the grounds (but not the argument) on which the party challenges the award and contends that permission should be given;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.1] (3) be accompanied by a skeleton argument in support of the application in accordance with paragraph 12.2; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.1] (4) append the award.

## 12.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.2] Subject to paragraph 12.3, the skeleton argument –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.2] (1) must be printed in 12 point font, with 1� line spacing;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.2] (2) should not exceed 15 pages in length; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.2] (3) must contain an estimate of how long the court is likely to need to deal with the application on the papers.

## 12.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.3] If the skeleton argument exceeds 15 pages in length the author must write to the court explaining why that is necessary.

## 12.4

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.4] Written evidence may be filed in support of the application only if it is necessary to show (insofar as that is not apparent from the award itself) –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.4] (1) that the determination of the question raised by the appeal will substantially affect the rights of one or more of the parties;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.4] (2) that the question is one which the tribunal was asked to determine;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.4] (3) that the question is one of general public importance;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.4] (4) that it is just and proper in all the circumstances for the court to determine the question raised by the appeal.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.4] Any such evidence must be filed and served with the arbitration claim form.

## 12.5

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.5] Unless there is a dispute whether the question raised by the appeal is one which the tribunal was asked to determine, no arbitration documents may be put before the court other than –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.5] (1) the award; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.5] (2) any document (such as the contract or the relevant parts thereof) which is referred to in the award and which the court needs to read to determine a question of law arising out of the award.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.5] In this Practice Direction ‘arbitration documents’ means documents adduced in or produced for the purposes of the arbitration.

## 12.6

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.6] A respondent who wishes to oppose an application for permission to appeal must file a respondent’s notice which –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.6] (1) sets out the grounds (but not the argument) on which the respondent opposes the application; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.6] (2) states whether the respondent wishes to contend that the award should be upheld for reasons not expressed (or not fully expressed) in the award and, if so, states those reasons (but not the argument).

## 12.7

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.7] The respondent’s notice must be filed and served within 21 days after the date on which the respondent was required to acknowledge service and must be accompanied by a skeleton argument in support which complies with paragraph 12.2 above.

## 12.8

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.8] Written evidence in opposition to the application should be filed only if it complies with the requirements of paragraph 12.4 above. Any such evidence must be filed and served with the respondent’s notice.

## 12.9

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.9] The applicant may file and serve evidence or argument in reply only if it is necessary to do so. Any such evidence or argument must be as brief as possible and must be filed and served within 7 days after service of the respondent’s notice.

## 12.10

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.10] If either party wishes to invite the court to consider arbitration documents other than those specified in paragraph 12.5 above the counsel or solicitor responsible for settling the application documents must write to the court explaining why that is necessary.

## 12.11

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.11] If a party or its representative fails to comply with the requirements of paragraphs 12.1 to 12.9 the court may penalise that party or representative in costs.

## 12.12

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.12] The court will normally determine applications for permission to appeal without an oral hearing but may direct otherwise, particularly with a view to saving time (including court time) or costs.

## 12.13

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.13] Where the court considers that an oral hearing is required, it may give such further directions as are necessary.

## 12.14

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.14] Where the court refuses an application for permission to appeal without an oral hearing, it will provide brief reasons.

## 12.15

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 12.15] The bundle for the hearing of any appeal should contain only the claim form, the respondent’s notice, the arbitration documents referred to in paragraph 12.5, the order granting permission to appeal and the skeleton arguments.

## SECTION II

## 13.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 13.1] This Section of this Practice Direction applies to arbitration claims to which Section II of Part 62 applies.

## 62.13 – Starting the claim

## 14.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 14.1] An arbitration claim must be started in the Commercial Court and, where required to be heard by a judge, be heard by a judge of that court unless he otherwise directs.

## SECTION III

## 15.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 15.1] This Section of this Practice Direction applies to enforcement proceedings to which Section III of Part 62 applies.

## 62.21 – Registration of awards under the Arbitration (International Investment Disputes) Act 1966

## 16.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 62 > 16.1] Awards ordered to be registered under the 1966 Act and particulars will be entered in the Register kept for that purpose at the Admiralty and Commercial Registry.
